title.rendered: Tshwane unveils digital dashboard in a pioneering effort to combat water losses

content.rendered:
Media Statement                                                                                17 October 2025

Cllr Frans Boshielo

MMC for Utility Services

 

A new public-private partnership introduces an innovative web-based platform to track water consumption vs losses to manage the demand.

The City of Tshwane has launched a state-of-the-art water balance dashboard in collaboration with Vodacom, the Strategic Water Partnership Network (SWPN), and Mezzanine. This web-based platform accessed on the City of Tshwane website (www.tshwane.gov.za), forms a key part of the city’s strategy to monitor water consumption and losses, and manage demand, in order to minimise non-revenue water (NRW), supporting its commitment to the Department of Water and Sanitation’s (DWS) “No Drop” programme for improved water efficiency and loss management.

This digital solution marks a shift towards data-driven water management, offering greater transparency and accountability. Using the International Water Association (IWA) water balance methodology, the system provides precise insight into water demand and losses, moving beyond the vague concept of Non-Revenue Water.

The dashboard will enable the city to identify water demand and losses areas by breaking down total water supplied per distribution networks. Boost public engagement by sharing data openly to help residents understand water consumption patterns and demand to foster collaborative efforts towards water conservation.

This initiative reflects a strong public-private partnership where the City of Tshwane leads the operational framework and implementation of DWS guidelines. Vodacom serves as technology partner and sponsor, supporting delivery through its subsidiaries, and SWPN & Mezzanine, in collaboration with GLS Consulting, provide the digital platform and analytics expertise to turn data into actionable insights.

Councillor Frans Boshielo, Member of the Mayoral Committee (MMC) for Utility Services at the City of Tshwane, stated:
“The introduction of the digital water tower is a transformative step for Tshwane.” It provides us with the opportunity to be transparent and accountable, which is fundamental to water conservation, revenue enhancement, and most critically delivering a more reliable service. Achieving ‘No Drop’ status and securing water for future generations is now a tangible, achievable target.

“Our partnership with Vodacom, the SWPN, and Mezzanine lays the foundation for a water-secure future. This initiative is about more than technology; it is about fundamentally reshaping how Tshwane stewards its most essential resource. By maximising from our own dams and boreholes, every drop saved moves us closer to water security. The journey towards a sustainable Tshwane begins with this decisive action.”

Martha Lamola, Operations Director for Vodacom Ventures and Partnerships, said:
“Vodacom’s purpose is to connect everyone for a better future. For us, that means genuinely improving quality of life. We understand that reliable, clean water is a critical foundation for this. This project puts our purpose into action, using technology and partnerships to champion water stewardship. We’re proud to be a sponsor and a long-term partner in this vital work.”

Alyssa Jooste, AB InBev Global Water and Nature Manager / SWPN Private Sector Co-Chair, said:
“The launch of this digital platform is a significant milestone for the SWPN, showcasing the powerful results of genuine public-private partnership. The No Drop Programme, developed collaboratively with the Department of Water and Sanitation through our working group, has been transformed into a practical tool delivering tangible impact. We are confident that the success seen in Tshwane will serve as a blueprint for other municipalities, accelerating our shared progress toward a water-secure future for South Africa.”

Jacques de Vos, CEO of Mezzanine, said:
“Mezzanine’s mission is to enable productive societies across Africa. We recognise that access to clean water is a fundamental prerequisite for all other community development. The challenges in regions like Gauteng extend beyond physical infrastructure; they require smart, non-infrastructure solutions that enhance revenue collection, guide strategic investment, and optimise daily operations. The Digital Water Tower is a critical building block in this effort, providing the actionable insights needed for informed decision-making. We applaud the vision of our partners in driving this initiative and are proud to contribute to its success.”

title.rendered: City of Tshwane payroll fraud crackdown nets imposter at its water facility – 17 August 2025

content.rendered:
The City of Tshwane’s Ethics Management and Forensic Services Division, working closely with the Tshwane Metro Police Department (TMPD), has discovered and exposed an individual posing as a legitimate employee at the City’s Rietvlei Water Treatment Plant.

The meticulously planned operation by the Ethics Management and Forensic Services Division followed a request from the Office of the Chief Operations Officer to investigate suspicions of identity fraud involving a staff member known at work as “Prince”. Investigations revealed that the individual had been employed by the City in 2012 under the name Mr Mohlaume Geoffrey Mamabolo, despite discrepancies regarding the official identity document on file.

The Department of Home Affairs confirmed that the genuine Mr Mamabolo’s identity document was issued in 2013, and the identity number in question had been blocked after “Prince” attempted to apply for a smart identity card. His fingerprints did not match the records in the Department of Home Affairs database, raising suspicions that he might be a foreign national.

In the early hours of Friday, 15 August 2025, the Ethics Management and Forensic Services Division, supported by TMPD members, confronted “Prince” at the water treatment plant. He failed to provide a valid explanation for the identity document discrepancy, could not give details of his upbringing or schooling, and ultimately admitted that he was not Mr Mamabolo. He further disclosed that the fraudulent identity document had been given to him years ago by an individual in Polokwane.

Investigators also discovered that “Prince” had no fixed address and had been residing on municipal property since his employment. Given the prima facie evidence of stolen identity, misrepresentation, contravention of the Immigration Act, 2002 (Act 13 of 2002) and fraud, TMPD officers arrested him and handed him over to the South African Police Service (SAPS) in Lyttelton. He is expected to appear in the Pretoria Magistrates’ Court on Monday, 18 August 2025.

The arrest was executed swiftly due to the security risk of his continued presence posed at the water treatment facility. The Office of the Chief Operations Officer, in conjunction with Group Human Capital Management, will institute appropriate labour relations processes to address the matter further.

This operation forms part of a broader fraud detection review of the City’s payroll system aimed at rooting out “ghost employees” and verifying the validity of all employees’ identity numbers.

The City extends its gratitude to the TMPD for its participation in the operation and for working alongside the Ethics Management and Forensic Services Division to facilitate training that will empower members of this division to be designated as peace officers in the fight against financial crime.

The forensic investigation is ongoing to determine how the suspect secured employment with fraudulent documentation.

The City Manager, Mr Johann Mettler, stated that “This arrest sends a strong message that the City of Tshwane will not tolerate fraud or misrepresentation in its ranks. We are tightening our systems to ensure that every person on our payroll is a legitimate employee who has been properly vetted.”

Mr Mettler further emphasised that the integrity of the City of Tshwane’s critical facilities, such as water treatment plants, cannot be compromised and that that our priority is to safeguard public resources and protect service delivery by removing individuals who infiltrate the system through fraudulent means.

title.rendered: Rand Water completes its maintenance of Hartebeeshoek Reservoir which supplies water to parts of Tshwane    18 July 2025

content.rendered:
The City of Tshwane has been informed by Rand Water that the cleaning, maintenance and inspection of its Hartebeeshoek Reservoir has been completed. The water utility’s team of technicians managed to complete the work on time. The maintenance started on Thursday, 3 July 2025, and was anticipated to take 16 days, with the last day being today, Friday, 18 July 2025.

During the maintenance period, various areas in Region 1 experienced a water supply interruption, which compelled the City to dispatch water tankers to the affected areas.

Rand Water currently supplies the Tshwane reservoirs through the bypass system, while simultaneously working on filling Hartebeeshoek Reservoir. According to Rand Water, supplying directly through the reservoir at this stage would significantly delay the network recovery. Consequently, both processes are being conducted in parallel to optimise supply restoration.

At this moment, the City’s reservoirs which are fed by Hartebeeshoek Reservoir are empty. However, it is reassuring to note that the City’s distribution network has started to fill up. Once the network is fully pressurised, the levels of the reservoirs will start picking up.

Residents are urged to exercise patience during the supply restoration period, as the network takes time to recover before it reaches the required pressure.

The City once more pleads with residents in low-lying areas to use water sparingly when the supply is restored in order to allow the system to reach a level at which high-lying areas will be able to get supply.

The City of Tshwane will continue to provide water through roaming water tankers to the affected customers until such time that the supply has been fully restored.

The City apologises for the inconvenience caused by this essential maintenance work.

title.rendered: Scheduled maintenance of Montana Reservoir

content.rendered:
As part of the ongoing operation and maintenance of the bulk water supply system, regular cleaning of storage reservoirs is essential to ensure water quality and system integrity. In line with the maintenance schedule as well as recent reports of water discoloration, Montana Reservoir is due for urgent cleaning and will undergo a full wash from 12 to 14 May 2025.

During this period, residents in the Montana Reservoir zone will continue to receive water through a temporary bypass pipeline. However, this pipeline has a lower capacity than the reservoir and may not fully meet peak demand. As a result, consumers are strongly urged to use water sparingly throughout the maintenance period.

title.rendered: TEMPORARY SHUTDOWN OF BRONKHORSTSPRUIT WATER TREATMENT PLANT

content.rendered:
Media alert
29 April 2025

The City of Tshwane will temporarily shut down Bronkhorstspruit Water Treatment Plant in order to facilitate the installation of new panels for the high-lift motors. This inevitable shutdown is scheduled to start on 5 May and will continue until 16 May 2025.

In a water treatment plant, panels for high-lift motors serve to control and monitor the operation of pumps that lift treated water to a higher elevation, typically for distribution to water towers or directly into the water reticulation system. These panels are crucial for ensuring efficient and reliable operation of the high-lift pumps, which are essential for delivering water to end users. This essential upgrade is aimed at enhancing the performance of the mentioned high-lift pumps.

The City intends to complete the upgrade within the specified period and will closely monitor and update residents on developments.

The following areas in Region 7 will be affected:

• Bronkhorstspruit Town
• Ekandustria
• Ekangala
• Rethabiseng
• Riamarpark
• Zithobeni
• Thembisile Hani Local Municipality (cross-border water supply)
The City of Tshwane sincerely apologises for the inconvenience that may be encountered as a result of this temporary shutdown.

Roaming water tankers have been arranged for all affected areas.

Issued by Communication, Marketing and Events.

title.rendered: Tshwane’s highest water consuming areas are likely to experience prolonged water supply interruptions

content.rendered:
The City of Tshwane has identified its highest consuming areas which are likely to put consumers at risk of experiencing consistent water supply interruptions. The demand in the identified areas is exceeding what the City can provide.

title.rendered: Rietvlei Water Treatment Plant update

content.rendered:
The City of Tshwane Rietvlei Water Treatment Plant, which has been offline for a few days following a lightning strike in the plant’s proximity, has now partially resumed operations.

This comes after the City’s technicians managed to effect repairs and replacements on some of the affected components of the Programmable Logic Controller (PLC), which is responsible for the plant’s automatic operation.

The plant, which supplies bulk water to the Garsfontein and Klapperkop Reservoirs, is currently only able to provide 7% of the daily water supply to Garsfontein Reservoir, as compared to the normal 9%. The supply to Klapperkop Reservoir will be initiated as soon as the plant’s pumping capacity, which is dependent on the completion of repairs, increases.

The Garsfontein and Klapperkop Reservoirs collect just over 9% and 10%, respectively, of their daily water intake from Rietvlei Water Treatment Plant. The rest of the supply comes from the Rand Water system.

The estimated time of the plant returning to full operation will only be determined once the repairs to the PLC have been completed.

Residents are urged to use water sparingly to ease pressure on the water network, which is under strain due to the high levels of consumption.

title.rendered: Mabopane area water challenges and interventions

content.rendered:
Media statement                                                                                                 12 February 2025
Cllr Frans Boshielo
MMC for Utility Services

Following multiple complaints from the community in the affected wards, I, as the MMC for
Utility Services, recognise the urgency of addressing the ongoing water issues in Mabopane.
Access to clean running water is a fundamental right, and we are committed to a thorough
investigation in order to resolve this matter effectively.

While the Water and Sanitation Department continues to provide water tankers as a relief
measure, we are actively working on a long-term solution.

Water tankers have been deployed to the following affected wards as temporary relief:
1. Ward 21: Cllr Phumzile
2. Ward 19: Cllr Mazibuko
3. Ward 12: Cllr Tsela
4. Ward 20: Cllr Neo
5. Ward 24: Cllr Masia

We want to assure both councillors and their communities that Mabopane remains a priority.
Our teams are conducting a thorough investigation in order to implement a lasting solution,
rather than relying on temporary fixes based on past advisories, which have often led to
unsustainable interventions. This will be closely monitored by the office of the MMC in
collaboration with Water and Sanitation Department officials.

Our investigation into the drop in reservoir levels over the past week revealed that critical
valves that supply the reservoir were vandalised. Since the system is pressurised by Rand
Water, we have requested them to isolate the supply so that our teams can carry out the
necessary repairs. However, gaining access to the reservoirs has been challenging, as our
workers have faced threats while attempting to conduct repairs.

To ensure the safety of our employees, we are engaging with the Tshwane
Metro Police Department (TMPD) for security support, in line with the
Occupational Health and Safety Act, 1993 (Act 85 of 1993). Vandalism remains
an issue, and we are working on community engagement with the TMPD to
assist with initiatives to raise awareness about its impact on essential services.

We appreciate the patience and cooperation of residents as we work to restore
consistent water supply to Mabopane. Further updates will be communicated
as progress is made.

This administration will strive to ignite service excellence.

title.rendered: Themba Water Treatment Plant still not fully functional

content.rendered:
Themba Water Treatment Plant is currently operating at half capacity following a power failure at the plant’s raw water abstraction point on 5 January 2025.

Both raw water pumps at the treatment plant were affected by the power outage, prompting the City’s technicians to temporarily shut the plant down.

The City’s team of technicians, who worked around the clock to get the pumps back into operation, managed to complete repairs on one of the two pumps. The repaired pump is now able to abstract raw water in order to feed the plant’s treatment section. The on-site reservoirs, which are fed by the treatment section, are slowly showing signs of improvement since pumping began earlier today.

However, consumers who are supplied by the plant’s Themba North Reservoir, are likely to experience low water pressure to no water as the reservoir’s level is still low. Areas that may be affected are Sekampaneng and Renstown.

Residents are advised to continue using water sparingly and to report any water leakages.

title.rendered: Rietgat Waste Water Treatment Works site inspection

content.rendered:
We visited Rietgat Waste Water Treatment Works (WWTW) located in Soshanguve Block HH to conduct a site inspection. Rietgat WWTW treats domestic sewage from surrounding areas. Upon arrival, it was found that effluent is discharged into Soutpanspruit, which flows through a nature reserve and ultimately into Klipvoordam in Limpopo, where Magalies Water purifies the water for drinking purposes.

Rietgat WWTW has suffered multiple acts of vandalism since August 2021 when the plant was severely damaged and key infrastructure was stolen, rendering it inoperable.

On 11 August 2023, security guards were held hostage at gunpoint while thieves stole cables, once again disrupting operations. Further, on 21 November 2023, a security guard was tragically killed during another vandalism incident.

These acts of vandalism have had the following significant consequences:

  • Environmental impact: Untreated sewage poses a serious threat to the environment, impacting Soutpanspruit, Klipvoordam and, ultimately, the drinking water supply.
  • Financial burden: The City has incurred substantial costs to repair Rietgat WWTW. The estimated repair costs exceed R8 million.

The City has contracted a firm to repair the infrastructure and replace the stolen and damaged equipment. The estimated completion date for the repairs and full operational restoration of Rietgat WWTW is 30 June 2025.

We strive to ignite service excellence.

title.rendered: City of Tshwane lodges notice of application with the Labour Court for the review of an Arbitration Award in respect of the suspended officials implicated in the Rooiwal Waste Water Treatment Works tender award

content.rendered:
The City of Tshwane has lodged a notice of application with the Labour Court for the review and setting aside of the outcome of the South African Local Government Bargaining Council (SALGBC) arbitration award, which ordered that the five senior employees who were charged with allegations of misconduct in the Rooiwal tender award should return to work by tomorrow, 20 January 2025.

After giving time and attention to the arbitration award and its implications, the City is of the view that there were defects in the proceedings and the ruling. The City is obligated to challenge the ruling and has enlisted the services of a firm of attorneys to act on its behalf in the handling of this legal matter.

The lodging of the notice of application against the SALGBC award freezes the legal effect the ruling has in its entirety.

Last year, the City filed an application with the Labour Court for a review of the findings and a sanction pronounced by the Chairperson of the disciplinary hearing. The matter is still pending before court and the City has petitioned the court to expedite the review application.

title.rendered: City of Tshwane declares water safe for human consumption in Hammanskraal areas that are part of Module 1 of the Klipdrift Package Plant

content.rendered:
The Hammanskraal intervention project has reached a critical milestone following the successful completion of the flushing of the City of Tshwane-managed and -operated reticulation system. This heralds a new beginning for the community of Hammanskraal which has not received water supply that is clean and safe for consumption for several years. This was further compounded by the cholera outbreak in May 2023, which led to loss of life and resulted in heightened fear from the community in terms of consuming water directly from the reticulation system.

While there had been delays in ensuring that communities receive water which is safe for human consumption as soon as possible, water quality assurance procedures could not be circumvented to achieve this objective. As required by law, substantial measures had to be undertaken to ensure that the reliable provision of potable water materialises.

At the core of this objective was flushing the reticulation system by removing sediment, debris and biofilm, optimising system operations for efficiency and conducting rigorous and consistent monitoring of water quality targets. This was done to ensure that the water supplied into the reticulation system does not pose any health risks to the public, which may lead to waterborne diseases given the associated sensitivities and history of water challenges in Hammanskraal.

The primary objective was to guarantee compliance with the SANS 241:2015 drinking water standard, ensuring the safety and suitability of the water for consumption. The City of Tshwane is pleased to announce that the affected distribution system has been successfully and thoroughly flushed. As a result, the water is fully compliant with the SANS 241:2015 standards for potable water quality. This achievement underscores Magalies Water’s commitment to delivering safe, clean and reliable drinking water, ensuring that the water supplied to our consumers meets the highest standards for human consumption.

In addition to this, the newly completed module of the package plant is tested on an ongoing basis to ensure that the water produced complies with the physical, chemical and microbiological specifications as outlined in SANS 241:2015. The evaluation focuses on verifying the system’s capabilities to meet all required parameters necessary for safe drinking water.

Post-flushing water quality evaluations were conducted. The findings of the final reports indicate that the system meets and surpasses the regulatory standards for potable water as outlined in SANS 241:2015. A comprehensive summary of the results is presented in Table I below.

Table I: Water quality performance against set SANS 241:2015 target for each risk parameter

Acute 2 health risk 100% 100% ≥99%

Operational risk 100% 97,28% ≥95%
Aesthetic health risk 100% 100% ≥95%

Considering the level of public interest in this intervention project and in promoting transparency and accountability, Magalies Water can readily avail comprehensive water quality test results upon request. This report was issued by a facility accredited under ISO/IEC 17025 standards as declared by the South African National Accreditation System (SANAS) and is free of any bias and/or influence.

The areas that will receive water include Mandela Village, Marokolong, Ramotse, Kekana Gardens (also referred to as Steve Bikoville) and Babelegi Industrial. As a risk abatement and management strategy, continuous monitoring and analysis of the water quality will be implemented throughout the entire water value chain to point of use. The main objective is to ensure that the water supplied in these areas consistently conforms to SANS 241:2015. Residents from these areas are reminded that billing for water will be effective immediately.

The Department of Water and Sanitation, the Gauteng Provincial Government, the City of Tshwane and Magalies Water will continue to work together to address the water situation in Hammanskraal. This progress is evidence of the government’s efforts to ensure that effective and efficient service delivery is realised through collaboration and cooperation among various spheres of government working together emboldened by the objectives of the intergovernmental relations framework.

South Africa remains a water-scare country and the supply remains constrained due to a combination of factors. Residents are encouraged to report incidents of infrastructure vandalism and illegal connections. Water is life and therefore all residents must have universal access to this all-important resource to ensure that the government achieves United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goal 6 on water and sanitation, as well as the country’s objectives in the National Development Plan (2030), which aims to accelerate access to potable water and its efficient use to promote inclusive economic growth.

title.rendered: City of Tshwane confirms safety of water supplied to some areas in Hammanskraal following laboratory-approved testing

content.rendered:
Media statement                                                                                                                                  8 January 2025
Cllr Nasiphi Moya
Executive Mayor of Tshwane

The City of Tshwane’s mayoral executive is pleased to inform residents of Hammanskraal that the water supplied from the Magalies Klipdrift Water Treatment Plant is safe for consumption, following the completion of Phase 1 of the project last year.

This announcement follows extensive testing conducted by the City, Magalies Water and the national Department of Water and Sanitation. The latest laboratory tests confirm that the water now meets all the required health standards for consumption.

This comes after a process of purging the reticulation system, which was previously supplied by Temba Water Works, using clean water sourced from the new Klipdrift Package Plant. The purpose of the prolonged purging process and accompanying inspections was to ensure that the system is fully rehabilitated, disinfected and safe.

The completion of the first phase of the project means that at least 12,5 megalitres per day (Mℓ/d) of treated water will be supplied to various areas in Hammanskraal. The supply areas include Wards 49, 73, 74 and 75, specifically Mandela Village, Marokolong, Ramotse, Kekana Gardens (also referred to as Steve Bikoville) and Babelegi Industrial.

The successful delivery of services to Hammanskraal forms part of long-term projects by the City and the national government to ensure that the quality of water provided to this community meets the constitutional obligations enjoyed by many citizens in the country.

The Magalies Water Klipdrift package project consists of four phases estimated to be completed in mid-2025. With the completion of each stage, more areas in Hammanskraal will benefit. This will be complemented by upgrades to Rooiwal Waste Water Treatment Plant (WWTP) being conducted by the City. The combination of these two projects will allow communities to benefit from a reliable and clean water supply.

It is a great injustice that this basic human right was absent for years in this community – a failure that was compounded by serious allegations of corruption surrounding the Rooiwal WWTP upgrade tender.

Earlier this week, the Special Investigating Unit confirmed that it has completed the first stage of its investigation into the Rooiwal WWTP tender. This has reportedly resulted in criminal referrals to the National Prosecuting Authority and disciplinary referrals to the City of Tshwane.

The mayoral executive welcomes the news of the completion of the first part of the investigation and is awaiting formal communication from the Special Investigating Unit to the City. We look forward to receiving the report and acting on its recommendations.

Addressing the injustice of the failure to provide potable water to the residents of Hammanskraal must include consequence management for the failures and corruption of the initial project. The completion of the first part of the investigation by the Special Investigating Unit brings us one step closer to ensuring accountability.

We thank residents for their patience during the process of ensuring the safety of the water and will continue to work with Magalies Water and the Department of Water and Sanitation to successfully deliver the future phases of the project.

Zintle Mahlati
zintlema@tshwane.gov.za

title.rendered: City of Tshwane reservoirs show stability as the festive season peaks, but residents should continue using water wisely

content.rendered:
Media statement                                                                                                                                        20 December 2024
Cllr Nasiphi Moya
Executive Mayor of Tshwane

 

Following weeks of water shortage issues reported across our regions, I am pleased to report that most of our City’s reservoirs are healthy and steady as residents gear up for the festive season.

In a report presented during the Mayoral Committee’s weekly service delivery war room, the Water and Sanitation Department reported that most reservoirs were all reporting at above 50% capacity on 20 December 2024.

The City of Tshwane relies on water received from Rand Water-managed supply systems, Palmiet and Mapleton. If these systems experience issues, the City is unable to supply water to reservoirs that are scattered across our regions. Some regions have problematic reservoirs, mostly located in Regions 1, 3 and 4.

Water supply to areas in Soshanguve are often affected by pumping issues at Soshanguve L, Soshanguve L Tower, Soshanguve DD, Mabopane, Laudium, Atteridgeville HL and Lotus Gardens are also prone to disruptions.

The reason why these reservoirs struggle is because of high consumption, overpopulation, increased water demand, illegal connections and vandalism.

Updated reservoir levels:

• Laudium – 70%
• Pretoria West High Lands – 62%
• Soshanguve DD – 67%
• Soshanguve L – 60%
• Soshanguve L Tower – 99%

We have made several interventions in some areas to help augment supply to areas that have lower supply levels. In Nellmapius, the supply was slightly restricted to boost supply to Mamelodi reservoirs.

We caution residents to use water responsibly during the festive season. Gauteng is experiencing water shortages, and it is imperative that we are all mindful of how we can help save water.

• Do not water or irrigate gardens with a hosepipe or sprinkler system between 05:00 and 18:00.
• Do not use a hosepipe to clean cars.
• Do not fill or top up swimming pools or water features.

title.rendered: BURGLARY INCIDENT AT NELLMAPIUS CLINIC IN MAMELODI

content.rendered:
The MMC for Health in the City of Tshwane condemns the burglary incident that took place at Nellmapius Clinic in Mamelodi in the early hours of today. We have been informed that unknown individuals unlawfully entered the clinic premises, resulting in a significant security breach.

The burglars accessed the facility by climbing the perimeter fence and breaking through a small aluminium window located in the back room, allowing them entry into the clinic. This break-in led to the theft of six computers, several headsets and the complete set of clinic keys, which poses a risk of granting the perpetrators full access to the clinic. In addition to the theft, three doors, including the one to the reception area, were damaged during this incident.

This burglary occurred despite the presence of two 24-hour security guards on-site. It is deeply concerning to note that this marks the fifth burglary incident at Nellmapius Clinic. We have launched a comprehensive investigation into the matter to identify and apprehend those responsible and to prevent any future incidents.

We call upon the community to assist us in this investigation. If anyone has any information that could help in identifying the culprits or recovering the stolen property, we urge you to come forward. Clinics are essential for servicing the health needs of our community and it is crucial that they remain secure and operational.

The City of Tshwane is committed to ensuring the safety and security of all healthcare facilities. We are currently reviewing our security protocols and will implement necessary enhancements to protect our clinics.

We appreciate the community’s support and cooperation in helping us maintain a secure and efficient healthcare environment. Together, we can overcome this challenge and continue to provide essential health services to the residents of Tshwane.

For further information, please contact the City of Tshwane Health Department.

title.rendered: Tshwane reservoirs gradually recovering

content.rendered:
The City of Tshwane is delighted to notice a significant improvement in most of the reservoir levels after some of them ran empty last week after a power trip struck Rand Water’s Palmiet Booster Pump Station on Wednesday, 6 November 2024.

The water supply to Thatchfield Ridge has been restored, albeit at low pressure. Parts of Olievenhoutbosch have also been restored, also at low pressure. Both areas are supplied by the Kosmosdal Meter. The City’s distribution team is currently releasing air within the network which is supplied directly by the Kosmosdal Meter.

The low-lying areas that are supplied by Atteridgeville LL Reservoir are also receiving water while the levels of The Reeds Reservoir, which stabilised over the weekend, have continued to increase. The reservoir is sitting well above 60%.

It is also encouraging to observe that the Atteridgeville HL and Laudium systems are showing signs of stability. All areas supplied by Laudium Reservoir have been restored.

Since this morning, the City’s technicians have been working on releasing air within the Atteridgeville HL system. The process is proving to be effective as Kalafong Heights is now receiving water, even though some households are still without supply. Efforts to restore Kalafong Hospital and Kwaggasrand are continuing.

The Mabopane system remains stable with most of the areas having been restored. Soshanguve L Reservoir is slowly recovering and pumping operations to the tower have resumed. Areas that are supplied by Soshanguve L Reservoir have been restored. Some customers who are supplied by the tower have started to receive water, even though the pressure is low. The pressure is expected to increase as and when the tower levels increase.

The levels of the Lotus and the Kruisfontein Reservoirs are still critically low. The distribution teams are continuously monitoring the systems for potential improvements.

The enlisting of interventions by the City of Tshwane political executive and senior management from the intergovernmental level is bearing fruit.

title.rendered: City of Tshwane reservoirs still at extremely low levels

content.rendered:
Media statement

 8 November 2024

City of Tshwane reservoirs that are supplied by Rand Water’s Klipriviersberg, Klipfontein, Brakfontein and Hartebeesthoek Reservoirs continue to experience extremely low levels or no water at all. This follows a power trip at the water utility’s Palmiet Booster Pump Station, which occurred on Wednesday, 6 November 2024.

This morning, Rand Water informed the City that it has now opened additional inlet valves into Hartebeesthoek Reservoir to increase its level to at least 40%. The utility is also removing airlocks in the system to intensify the recovery process. At 40%, the system will be pressurised enough to deliver water to Soshanguve L Reservoir. This move is also expected to assist in the recovery of Mabopane Reservoir and Kruisfontein Reservoir.

It is encouraging to note that low-lying areas in Atteridgeville have started to receive water. We urge those customers to use water sparingly in order to allow the system to recover.

The Olievenhoutbosch/Thatchfield system looks promising, but it has yet to stabilise. The Reeds Reservoir and Lotus Reservoir are still empty. The City’s team of technicians is currently in discussion with the Rand Water team to explore potential measures to address all our areas of concern.

The City once more urges customers to exercise patience during this difficult period, as the network takes time to fully recover. Residents will be kept updated as and when there are new developments.

The City apologises for the inconvenience caused by this unplanned water supply interruption.

Issued by Communication, Marketing and Events.

title.rendered: City of Tshwane apologises for delays in water restoration following Rand Water Palmiet Booster Pump Station interruption

content.rendered:
As MMC for Utility Services, I am deeply concerned that many residents of Tshwane continue to face water supply challenges despite the Rand Water Palmiet Booster Pump Station being back online.

The power failure at the Palmiet Booster Pump Station on Wednesday, 6 November 2024, led to a significant reduction in the water supply, impacting various reservoirs across the city. The affected reservoirs include Lotus, Mabopane, Soshanguve L, Laudium, Atteridgeville HL, Atteridgeville LL, The Reeds, Kruisfontein, and Klipgat.

While we welcomed the news that the power issue at the Palmiet Booster Pump Station was resolved and the station returned to full operational capacity by Thursday, many of our reservoirs remain at critically low levels.

Within the constraints of the interconnected supply system, my department has worked to redistribute water between systems to mitigate the impact. We have also implemented supply restrictions to most reservoirs to prevent a total system collapse.

However, there are certain areas, such as those fed by the Hartebeeshoek system – including Soshanguve L, which is currently without water – that rely solely on the recovery of the Palmiet system.

 

We urge residents who currently have water to use it sparingly to reduce pressure on the supply system and expedite recovery in areas that remain without water.

To support residents without access, water tankers have been deployed to affected areas, and efforts are ongoing to restore normal water supply as quickly as possible.

The City sincerely apologises for the inconvenience caused and appreciates your patience and cooperation as we work towards stabilising the water supply system.

Enquiries:

Johanna Phatshwane (johannaph@tshwane.gov.za)

title.rendered: City of Tshwane to restrict some reservoirs to stabilise the struggling ones

content.rendered:
The Tshwane water distribution network is faced with challenges due to high water demand in some parts of the city. To mitigate these challenges, the City will, where feasible, restrict healthy reservoirs within the system to assist the struggling ones with a view to balancing and stabilising the network.

This means that there will be no inflow of water to the throttled reservoirs. Their inlets will only be opened once the struggling ones have recovered.

This system alternation approach will be carried out daily until we have sufficient supply. It is under these circumstances that the City is once more imploring all consumers to conserve water to avoid prolonged water supply interruptions.

The City is currently implementing the alternation approach in the Laudium/Atteridgeville HL system which supplies Laudium, Atteridgeville, Kwaggasrand, West Park and surrounding areas.

Currently, the Heights Reservoir system levels are healthy and this will allow our team to begin supplementing supply to Laudium and Atteridgeville this evening.

The City urges all customers in the low-lying areas of the network, who will receive water first, to use it sparingly to allow for the gradual recovery of the reservoirs and to enable consumers in the high-lying zones to also receive water.

title.rendered: Temba Water Treatment Works to remain off pending raw water test results

content.rendered:
The City of Tshwane’s Temba Water Treatment Works that supplies water to Hammanskraal and surrounding areas will remain off pending the improvement of the water quality from the Leeuwkraal Dam, from which Temba Water Treatment Works sources its raw water for treatment to potable standards.

Temba Water Treatment Works was shut down on Monday, 7 October 2024, after the City’s technicians discovered that there was sewer contamination in the Leeuwkraal Dam. Pumping had to stop to avoid supplying poor water quality to our consumers.

These challenges were caused by a fire that gutted Pyramid Substation on 2 October 2024, leaving Rooiwal Waste Water Treatment Works without electricity. The plant had to temporarily cease operations and consequently discharged untreated sewage into the Apies River, which feeds the Leeuwkraal Dam.

In the interim, a team of scientists is monitoring the performance of Rooiwal Waste Water Treatment Works to ensure that it complies with the required effluent standards. These standards, mandated by strict regulatory requirements, include limits on chemical oxygen demand (COD), total suspended solids (TSS), nitrate (NO3), phosphate (PO4), ammonia, E. coli and residual chlorine which must be consistently met by the plant.

The City will continue to provide roaming water tankers to residents until the situation normalises. There are residents who have alleged that some water tankers were being channelled to “connected” people and, as a result, some communities do not receive water through the tankers.

Furthermore, some have alleged that they are being forced to pay to receive water. The City wishes to make it categorially clear that the City’s contracted service providers are delivering water for free and residents do not have to pay for it.

The City had initially made a commitment that the pumping of water would resume within seven days, however, this is dependent on the outcome of the laboratory tests. The City’s laboratory team, which took raw water samples from Temba Water Treatment Works for testing, is expected to release the results by the end of this week.

Residents will be kept updated as and when there are new developments.

The City apologises for the inconvenience that may have been caused as a result of this unplanned interruption.

content.rendered:
Tshwane is experiencing high water consumption in Atteridgeville and surrounding areas. As a result, this has led to an outage in the area distribution zone.

Residents in the supply area are thus encouraged to use water sparingly. With the spring season upon us, residents and the business community in the jurisdiction of the City of Tshwane are reminded to continue with their efforts to conserve water.

This period is typically associated with increased water consumption, which puts a strain on the water supply system. Water conservation means using our limited water supply wisely and making every effort to conserve it.

  • Do not water or irrigate gardens with hosepipes or sprinkler systems between 06:00 and 18:00.
  • Do not wash vehicles with hosepipes.
  • Do not fill swimming pools.
  • Install a low-flow shower head and tap aerators where possible.
  • Use a dual-flush toilet cistern.
  • Plant indigenous or drought-resistant shrubs in the garden.
  • Use a broom instead of a hosepipe when cleaning driveways or patios.
  • Collect rainwater to reuse in the garden or wash the car.
  • Cover the swimming pool to reduce water evaporation.
  • Take a short shower rather than a bath.
  • Close a running tap while brushing teeth or shaving.
  • Regularly check toilets and taps for leaks.

By adhering to water-saving hints, the City and Tshwane residents can contribute immensely to water conservation and safeguard water levels from deteriorating.

The City is once more urging those residents who still have access to water to use water sparingly and refrain from filling their storage tanks to allow the system to stabilise.

title.rendered: Land rehabilitation process underway in Pienaarspoort – Mamelodi flood victims relocation imminent

content.rendered:
Earlier today, I handed over the Pienaarspoort development site to a contractor where rehabilitation work is set to begin in preparation of the relocation of the Mamelodi flood victims.

Once the land was acquired by the provincial government, we discovered that the land in question had been used for extensive illegal sand mining activities and was thus unsuitable for habitation.

To correct this, the City appointed a service provider to clear the site and rehabilitate it to make it suitable for the affected families to receive serviced stands.

The site is currently being cleared and once all rehabilitation work is completed, it will yield more than 5 000 serviced stands to the Mamelodi flood victims and other informal settlements, including Eerstefabrieke, Soul City, Phomolong and others.

The Pienaarspoort relocation is an important milestone for the department and we aim to complete it before the rainy season begins to avoid another flood situation. With the groundwork now officially started, we envisage that relocations will begin in November 2024.

Once relocated, these households will receive rudimentary water and sewer services while we plan for bulk services to the area.

The City is thrilled to finally be at this stage where we can get this project underway.

title.rendered: City of Tshwane Health Department to host diabetes outreach in Mamelodi

content.rendered:
On 13 September 2024, the City of Tshwane Health Department will host the first of two diabetes outreach programmes for 2024. This first outreach programme will take place at Mamelodi West Community Hall.

Diabetes is considered as a chronic disease of public health concern. According to the national Department of Health, the three common categories of diabetes include Type 1, where the blood glucose (sugar) level is too high as the body produces very little or no insulin; Type 2, which is due to lifestyle factors such as obesity, lack of physical activity or hereditary factors; and Type 3, which is gestational diabetes mellitus. This temporary condition develops in women, mostly during pregnancy, and has the potential to cause health problems in both mother and baby. Untreated diabetes can lead to stroke, nerve damage, blindness, kidney failure, heart attack and amputations.

Given the seriousness of this disease, interested community members are encouraged to attend the outreach programme and learn about the available services on diabetes and the aspects of care for diabetic people as well as the comprehensive package of other health promotion services. In partnership with various stakeholders, the following services will be available on the day: Blood pressure and blood glucose screening, eyecare and footcare, oral health screening, tuberculosis and HIV screening, drug and substance use awareness, gender-based violence awareness, mental health awareness, occupational health, physiotherapy and nutrition information.

As a demonstration of our commitment to bring services closer to communities, we will be partnering with the following stakeholders and sponsors: The Gauteng Department of Health, Wits Reproductive Health and HIV Institute (Wits RHI), the Aurum Institute, the Moses Mabhida Foundation, Sungardens Palliative Care, Voice It In Action, Thandanani Drop Inn Centre, Phokwane Funeral Directors and Synexus.

These outreach programmes aim to highlight the importance of regular screening and testing related to health matters. Early detection can save lives.

The second diabetes outreach programme is planned for 25 October2024 at Hercules Clinic.

title.rendered: City of Tshwane on track to provide clean water in Hammanskraal

content.rendered:
Media statement                                                                                             20 August 2024

Ald Cilliers Brink

Executive Mayor of Tshwane

 

The City of Tshwane is pleased to announce significant progress in our ongoing efforts to deliver clean, potable water to the residents of Hammanskraal. During a recent community imbizo held on 17 August 2024 at Makgoba Sebothoma Hall in Hammanskraal, key updates were provided on the advancement of critical water infrastructure projects, including the Phase 1 upgrading of Klipdrift Water Treatment Plant and the Rooiwal Waste Water Treatment Plant.

The engagement provided a platform for residents to engage directly with the panel during a question-and-answer session, fostering an open dialogue about the project’s impact and progress.

The City remains vigilant in overseeing both Rooiwal Waste Water Treatment Plant and Klipdrift Water Treatment Plant projects. We are committed to addressing any potential delays and acts of sabotage and ensuring the appointment of credible contractors. We will continue to update residents on project progress and work towards eliminating the need for water tankers by ensuring clean, potable drinking water for all. Moving away from water tankers will enable us to repurpose aging infrastructure and advance service delivery.

We value the trust of our community and will continue to build and reaffirm this trust through transparent communication and dedicated efforts. As part of our efforts, we have completed a thorough audit of water meters across 37 620 households. Of these, 23 616 meters were found to be in good working order, while 14 004 meters are scheduled for replacement between September and November 2024.

Recognising the financial burden on our residents, we will be presenting some resolutions to Council on writing off historical debt associated with the audited meters. This decision will provide residents a fresh start with new potable tap water available in their homes, eliminating the reliance on water tankers.

I want to acknowledge the Deputy Mayor, Cllr Nasiphi Moya, and the MMC for Utilities and Regional Operations and Coordination, Cllr Themba Fosi, who have been conducting monthly oversight visits to keep regular watch on the projects and have been instrumental in ensuring that the City remains on track with our work to provide water to Hammanskraal residents.

I also want to thank the Speaker of Council, Cllr Mncedi Ndzwanana, for organising the community imbizo.

Our interventions in Hammanskraal represent the most significant progress made by any administration in the past 20 years.

title.rendered: City of Tshwane makes significant progress on provision of clean drinking water in Hammanskraal

content.rendered:
Media statement                                                                                             14 August 2024

Cllr Themba Fosi

MMC for Utilities and Regional Operations and Coordination

 

The City of Tshwane would like to provide a progress update on two critical projects aimed at improving water supply to our residents in Hammanskraal, namely Rooiwal Waste Water Treatment Plant and Magalies Water Package Plant that is meant to provide tap water as an interim measure while Rooiwal upgrades are underway.

Rooiwal Waste Water Treatment Plant progress

The Rooiwal Waste Water Treatment Plant upgrade is a key project in the City’s commitment to providing clean potable water to our residents. Construction has officially commenced, marking a significant step towards the City’s efforts to enhance the plant’s waste water treatment capacity.

To date, substantial progress has been made across various components of the project. The installation of the Clear Vu fence at both the north and east works is nearly complete, with 93% and 100% installed, respectively. Key mechanical and electrical repairs are underway, including the completion of blowers and belt press installations.

 Over the next three months, we anticipate advancing the construction of two primary sedimentation tanks, the refurbishment of the east flow balancing tank and pump station, and the upgrading of the anaerobic digesters at Rooiwal West Works.

Our teams are also focused on accelerating milestones to ensure timely completion, with additional resources being mobilised to fast-track cleaning and repairs.

The City is working in partnership with the Department of Water and Sanitation, the National Treasury and the Development Bank of Southern Africa, as the managing agent, in a collaborative effort to accelerate solutions to Hammanskraal’s water challenges.

Magalies Water Package Plant

While construction work is underway at Rooiwal, the City recognises that residents want water from their taps and not from water tankers. Therefore, as an interim measure, the City has partnered with Magalies Water and the Department of Water and Sanitation to deliver potable tap water to affected Hammanskraal areas.

As part of this intervention, the City has audited 37 620 households, with 23 616 water meters confirmed to be in good working condition. However, about 14 004 meters will be replaced between September and November 2024. This is a critical step in preparing for the supply of clean potable water from Magalies Water Package Plant to Hammanskraal residents, starting in September 2024.

The City has also taken a decision to write off historic debt associated with the audited meters, giving residents an opportunity to start afresh with new potable tap water available in their homes.

Community imbizo

To further engage with our residents and provide detailed updates, we will hold an imbizo on 17 August 2024. The Executive Mayor, Ald Cilliers Brink, the Deputy Mayor, Cllr Nasiphi Moya, Speaker of Council, Cllr Mncedi Ndzwanana along with myself as the MMC tasked with leading the department responsible for water services, will lead the City’s delegation and engage the community on the progress we are making.

The imbizo will provide information on the expected arrival date of clean water in Hammanskraal, starting in September 2024. We invite residents from the three affected wards to join us for this important engagement.

We remain committed to ensuring access to clean water for all residents and we are pleased by the progress made under this administration. Our interventions in Hammanskraal represent the most significant progress made by any administration in the past 20 years.

 Enquiries:

Tsebo Majoro

tseboma@tshwane.gov.za

title.rendered: Update on water outage in Tshwane following Rand Water’s infrastructure maintenance of its systems that supply bulk water to Gauteng metros

content.rendered:
The City of Tshwane is pleased to announce that there has been a gradual improvement in the City’s bulk and distribution systems which are fed by Rand Water’s Mapleton System.

The City’s system ran dry following Rand Water’s infrastructure maintenance work on its Mapleton System, which took 77 hours (three days and five hours) to be completed. This exercise started on Friday, 26 July 2024, and ended on Monday morning. During that period, there was no pumping to the Mapleton System. This left various areas in Regions 2, 3 and 6 without water, compelling the City to dispatch water tankers to the affected areas.

It is important to note that the City of Tshwane, like other metros in Gauteng, receives 79% of its bulk water supply from Rand Water’s two booster pumping stations, Mapleton and Palmiet. Rand Water has to first replenish its own reservoirs fed from the Mapleton and Palmiet Systems before it can begin to distribute water to its municipal customers.

This process can take up to two weeks for the network to fully recover. This, however, does not imply that the water supply will be restored in two weeks’ time.

It is encouraging to note that, even though the gradual build-up of the water supply is at a slow pace, some residents in the areas that were without water have confirmed water flowing from their taps.

The following areas have started to receive water:

  • Die Wilgers
  • Eersterust
  • Silverton
  • Waltloo
  • Wapadrand

The areas that are still without water will continue to be serviced by water tankers. The deployment of water trucks is being coordinated through the relevant ward councillors.

 The City is pleading once more with residents in the low-lying areas to use water sparingly when the supply is restored to allow our bulk water system and reservoirs to recover quickly.

The City apologises for the inconvenience caused by this planned water supply interruption.

title.rendered: Update on Rand Water’s infrastructure maintenance of its systems that supply water to the City of Tshwane

content.rendered:
Rand Water has notified the City of Tshwane that the infrastructure maintenance work on its Mapleton System has been completed. The water utility’s team of technicians managed to timeously complete the work, which started on Friday, 26 July 2024, and ended this morning. The maintenance period took 77 hours (three days and five hours) without any pumping.

During the maintenance period, various areas in Regions 2, 3 and 6 experienced water supply interruptions, compelling the City to dispatch water tankers to the affected areas. Currently, the City’s entire bulk and distribution systems that are fed by the Mapleton System are empty.

It is encouraging to note that Rand Water’s team is currently charging the pipelines. Once charging has been completed, pumping to the Mapleton System will resume. Residents are urged to exercise patience during the pumping period as the network takes two weeks to fully recover before it reaches the required pressure. The City will continue to provide water to its affected customers through roaming water tankers.

Rand Water is undertaking its final maintenance on the Palmiet System for 40 hours today from 05:00 until Tuesday, 30 July 2024, at 21:00. Pumping will be reduced to 76% during this period.

The City is pleading once more with residents in the low-lying areas to use water sparingly when the supply is restored to allow our bulk water system and reservoirs to recover quickly.

The City apologises for the inconvenience caused by this planned water supply interruption.

title.rendered: Update: Water supply interruption affecting Zithobeni and nearby areas

content.rendered:
This morning, a team of technicians from the City of Tshwane Bulk Water Supply Section commenced with the installation of a new pipe to replace the burst pipe that supplies Zithobeni Reservoir in Region 7.

The new pipe was delivered at the workshop for fabrication yesterday prior to installation. Subsequent to the installation of the new pipe, the team will proceed to the second part of the repair work, which is the connection of the y-pipe. If all goes well, it is estimated that all the work should be completed by this evening.

The City would like to alert customers that after the successful installation of the new pipe, technicians still have to test pumping, and because the reservoir and the network are empty, the pipeline will have to fill up first before the reservoir can start building up pressure.

The water supply will be restored gradually to the low-lying areas first before the high-lying areas can experience water flow from their taps.

It is unfortunate that our customers in Zithobeni had to endure a prolonged water outage following complications which developed when the City’s technicians were fixing a major leak on a main bulk pipeline that supplies Zithobeni Reservoir last week on Wednesday, 12 June 2024. These delays were not anticipated, however, the technical team is working around the clock to ensure that the water supply to the area is restored as soon as possible.

The City understands your frustrations and appreciates your patience during this very difficult period.

The City will retain the roaming water tankers in the affected areas until the water supply is fully restored. As and when the situation dictates, the City will consider increasing the number of tankers to meet the demand.

 Issued by Communication, Marketing and Events.

title.rendered: City of Tshwane cancels water tanker tender before it is awarded

content.rendered:
Media statement                                                                                                 18 June 2024

Cllr Jacqui Uys

MMC for Finance

Earlier this year, the City of Tshwane advertised a tender to appoint a panel for the supply of water tankers as rudimentary services in informal areas. The City has now taken decisive action to cancel this tender before the award to prevent any possible corruption.

This comes as a result of newly implemented corruption-detection mechanisms in supply chain processes, which flagged that there was a leak of valuation documentation and a possible compromise in the tender specifications.

The tender specifications will now be reworked and the tender re-advertised. This decision reflects the City’s unwavering commitment to upholding the highest standards of accountability, integrity and fairness in operations.

While this will not impact the current supply of water tankers, it does highlight the harsh reality that water, even as a basic human right, is used by some to enrich themselves.

The City’s political leadership is committed to stopping the exploitation of vulnerable and poor residents. In this regard, we have also made the decision to spend 30% of the funds allocated to water tanker provision in the 2024/25 financial year to explore sustainable, long-term solutions for the supply of water to informal areas.

title.rendered: City of Tshwane marks significant progress at Rooiwal Waste Water Treatment Plant

content.rendered:
On Friday, 7 June 2024, the City of Tshwane Rooiwal Subcommittee visited Rooiwal Waste Water Treatment Plant.

Along with my colleagues, Ald Hannes Coetzee and Cllr Themba Fosi, we were encouraged by the steady progress made by officials to ensure that Phase 1 of the refurbishment of Rooiwal is completed by April 2025.

The visit offered incredible insights into the tremendous progress being made in comparison to a previous visit conducted on 9 May 2024. There has been progress in securing the site with security personnel, with the future aim of installing camera surveillance. Other areas of improvement include equipment management and reinstallation, which have all been dealt with according to plan.

Other areas on track with the project plan include the completion of pumping sewage effluent and desludging. This means that the removal of scrapper down pipes and refurbishments will start this month.

When we handed the project over to the Development Bank of Southern Africa, we envisioned March 2025 as the deadline for general building and mechanical engineering and April 2025 for the Phase 1 completion deadline.

The importance of completing the refurbishments at Rooiwal will ensure that we can improve the quality of water that is discharged from the plant. Once the system runs steadily at the plant, we should be able to monitor the safety and quality of the water provided and its chemical distributions.

Our visit to Rooiwal also finalised the final steps to ensuring that Hammanskraal residents have access to clean water by September 2024. This deadline is still within our reach with the completion of the water meter readings project. Over 30 000 household meters were assessed during the programme.

We thank the residents of Hammanskraal for their cooperation and enabling us to complete our water meter audits two months ahead of schedule. We remain committed to exercising our political leadership to ensure the success of this project. The subcommittee will return to the area at the end of June 2024 for further oversight.

title.rendered: City of Tshwane and the Department of Water and Sanitation sign a Memorandum of Understanding to address the City’s water constraints

content.rendered:
The City of Tshwane has set the wheels in motion towards formalising strategic partnerships that will contribute towards addressing the City’s water and sanitation-related challenges.

The national Department of Water and Sanitation (DWS) is one of these strategic partners which the City has approached, not only to be involved as a regulator, but also to collaborate on issues such as leveraging DWS technical and financial resources to jointly address the City’s other challenges, such as the pollution of the Hennops River, upgrading Rooiwal Waste Water Treatment Works and inadequate human resources.

Today, 10 June 2024, the two parties signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to collaborate on various strategic areas, such as infrastructure planning and development, water resource planning and infrastructure solutions, and capacity-building of City of Tshwane officials. Discussions are at an advanced stage to finalise a flagship engineering candidacy development programme, which will see the secondment of candidate engineers to the City and professional engineers who will be contracted to the City for a three-year period. This team of engineers has undergone training under the DWS.

In addition, the DWS will offer free mentorship through its database of mentors to the candidate engineers to assist them to obtain their professional registration with the Engineering Council of South Africa (ECSA). Once implemented successfully, the programme will assist the City to comply with the new ECSA Identification of Engineering Work Regulations.

The MoU was signed by the City Manager of the City of Tshwane, Mr Johann Mettler, and DWS Deputy Director-General for Water and Sanitation Services, Dr Risimati Mathye, at the City’s headquarters, Tshwane House.

During the signing ceremony, Mettler said: “Addressing our major water challenges requires a collaborative effort between the City and key water stakeholders, and the DWS is one of those key players. We have been facing significant water challenges which have negatively affected some of our residents for a longer period. Some of these challenges can be linked to ageing infrastructure and maintenance challenges at some of our water treatment plants.”

Dr Mathye said that the collaboration between the two entities is a significant one, particularly on the DWS side, to fulfil its role as a regulator of the water and sanitation sector.

“We are pleased by the will and zeal that has been shown by the City in ensuring collaborative efforts and allowing us to work together in different spheres of government to ensure efficient services to the residents of Tshwane. It has always been our intention to work with all municipalities at local government level to capacitate them where we can to achieve Sustainable Development Goals, particularly Goal 6, to realise clean water and decent sanitation provision to communities,” Dr Mathye emphasized.

The other key areas of collaboration that the MoU will focus on include the following:

  • Water resource planning and infrastructure solutions in line with the City’s Climate Action Plan
  • Infrastructure planning and development
  • Collaboration on water and sanitation-related programmes
  • Sustainable Development Goal 6: Clean water and sanitation
  • Training and capacity-building, including secondment of staff between the parties
  • Education and awareness campaigns (such as National Water Week)
  • Knowledge-sharing (jointly hosting seminars and conferences)
  • Benchmarking programmes, such as Green Drop, Blue Drop and No Drop
  • Joint enforcement programmes to prevent water pollution
  • Exploration of alternative water and sanitation technologies with DWS and its entities
  • Key bulk infrastructure in line with the Metropolitan Spatial Development Framework and Regional Spatial Development Frameworks
  • Any other additional area that the parties may agree to collaborate on in future

The signed MoU reinforces the ideal of the Intergovernmental Relations Act, 2005 (Act 13 of 2005), which implores a concerted effort by government in all spheres to work together and to integrate, as far as possible, their actions in the provision of services, the alleviation of poverty and the development of society.

title.rendered: City makes progress towards the provision of clean water to Hammanskraal residents

content.rendered:
Media statement                                                                                                  13 May 2024

Cllr Nasiphi Moya

Deputy Mayor

In my capacity as Deputy Mayor, along with the MMC for Utilities and Regional Operations and Coordination, Cllr Themba Fosi, and the MMC for Region 2, Ald Hannes Coetzee, we conducted an oversight visit to the Rooiwal Infrastructure Upgrade Project on Friday.

Significant progress has been made, with both the general building and mechanical and electrical contractors on-site and actively working on an accelerated plan to enhance the efficiency and functionality of the plant.

One of the key milestones of this project is the assessment of the quality of the effluent discharged from the plant. Thanks to the proactive efforts of our contractors, we are optimistic that by December 2024 we will start having measurable data on the improved quality of the effluent being discharged.

In another crucial development, preparations are well underway to provide clean water to the residents of Hammanskraal by September 2024. We are proud to report that our audit team has successfully assessed over 23 000 households out of the initial target of 39 000. This puts us two months ahead of our scheduled timeline and demonstrates our commitment to delivering clean water to the community in a timely manner.

We remain dedicated to the successful completion of the Rooiwal Infrastructure Upgrade Project and pledge to continue working diligently towards achieving our goals. We appreciate the ongoing support of all stakeholders involved in this vital project.

title.rendered: City of Tshwane conducts water meter audits in Hammanskraal

content.rendered:
Media statement                                                                                                  16 April 2024

Cllr Nasiphi Moya

Deputy Mayor

Community and Social Development Services

The City of Tshwane is pleased to announce the commencement of a water meter audit drive in Hammanskraal this week. The initiative follows the recent launch of the Magalies Water Package Plant project, which aims to ensure clean water supply to the residents of Hammanskraal by September 2024.

The audit team has started their work in Hammanskraal West and is scheduled to cover all affected areas within Hammanskraal by 31 July 2024.

Following the auditing process, water meter replacements and new water meter installations will be concluded by 30 September 2024 as more meters might be identified for replacement during the audit.

As part of the meter audit process, City officials and contracted service providers will also do data collection in the area. This will involve activities such as opening and closing water taps, recording water meter numbers and readings, and confirming physical and street addresses.

The city calls on Hammanskraal residents to please cooperate with officials and service providers during the audit process. It is essential for residents to allow access to their yards for the necessary inspections. A successful audit will ensure that the City’s water systems are prepared to receive and supply water to the affected areas in Hammanskraal.

In my capacity as the Deputy Mayor together with MMC for Utility Services Cllr Themba Fosi, we will both play an oversight role over the meter auditing process in order ensure that we deliver metered drinking tap water for the people of Hammanskraal.

For confirmation of the auditors’ identities, residents can contact the City of Tshwane on 012 358 9062.

title.rendered: City of Tshwane condemns possible sabotage of water infrastructure in Rethabiseng

content.rendered:
The City of Tshwane, in the strongest possible terms, condemns probable acts of sabotage by characters who are depriving residents of their right to clean, potable water in and around the Rethabiseng area, which is situated between Bronkhorstspruit and Ekangala in Region 7.

Yesterday, 19 March 2024, the City reported that water had been restored in Ekangala and Rethabiseng, with the exception of Rethabiseng Ext 4, due to challenges experienced with the infrastructure network connection.

Some parts of Region 7, particularly Rethabiseng and Ekangala, had experienced a prolonged water outage caused by the breakdown of a pump at Bronkhorstspruit Water Treatment Plant. As a mitigating factor, water tankers were dispatched to the affected areas during that period.

Shortly after water supply had been restored and deployment of the water tankers was stopped, reports emerged from some quarters in the affected areas which indicate possible sabotage in the form of tampering with the City’s infrastructure.

Today, the City received information that a Mahindra bakkie which was spotted in Rethabiseng Ext 4 is suspected to be involved in meddling with water valves in the area. It is presumed that the alleged saboteurs of the water infrastructure are the drivers of the bakkie in question. This supposition is yet to be proven.

Officials from the Tshwane Metro Police Department (TMPD) have been activated to conduct operations in the area.

Residents are urged to write down the registration numbers of questionable vehicles and to report them immediately to the TMPD on 012 358 7095/7096. This number is manned 24/7.

Meanwhile, there were allegations earlier today that tap water in Riamarpark was brownish in colour, sparking fears of possible impurity. The City moved swiftly to conduct sampling in the said area, and it was discovered that the water is colourless.

The City of Tshwane calls on the clique allegedly involved in the disruption of clean, drinkable water in the region to immediately desist from doing so, as this not only threatens service delivery, but also endangers the health of residents.

 Issued by Communication, Marketing and Events.

title.rendered: City of Tshwane and Coca-Cola Beverages South Africa open a borehole in Gomora Informal Settlement

content.rendered:
Media statement                                                                                    19 March 2024

Cllr Ofentse Madzebatela

MMC for Human Settlements

 

On Monday 18 March 2024, I joined Coca-Cola Beverages South Africa (CCBSA) for the official opening of a borehole for the Malusi/Gomora Informal Settlement at the Malusi Youth Development Organisation Community Centre in Pretoria West.

The CCBSA approached the City’s Human Settlements Department with a proposal for a solar-powered groundwater-harvesting project to drill a borehole to partially address the water needs of the community.

Currently, the settlement receives rudimentary services through water tankers and chemical toilets in the absence of engineering services in the area. This is a result of the ongoing service delivery challenges in the area that continue to affect the provision of water to the community.

The opening of this borehole comes at a time where Gauteng is experiencing water-scarcity challenges. As a City, we welcome the innovative work by the CCBSA to address a social challenge in their community by maximising own water-generation capacity.

Equally important is that the location of the borehole forms part of the existing formalisation project located on the Remainder of Portion 21, 124, 150 and 227 of the farm Zandfontein 317-JR, also known as the proposed township Kirkney Ext 68, and will go a long way to provide safe drinking water to residents.

The City of Tshwane stands firm on our whole-of-society approach to better service delivery by working with businesses, communities and individuals to make a City that works for all its people.

We remain committed to address water challenges in informal areas and to provide clean and drinkable water to all residents of Tshwane.
